alerts.title: Significant Weight Gain and Metabolic Changes on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines note weight gain is a problem in HIV care, particularly among women, and should be discussed proactively. The patient has gained 17 kg (BMI increased from 25.6 to 32.4 kg/m²) over 18 months since switching to a DTG-based regimen (TLD). She now has obesity, acanthosis nigricans, pre-diabetes (fasting glucose 118 mg/dL, HbA1c 6.1%), and dyslipidemia. DTG is a known contributor to weight gain. However, family history of Type 2 diabetes is a non-drug risk factor. The patient also reports increased fatigue, which aligns with metabolic syndrome.

evidence.recommended_action: Discuss weight gain risk, provide diet and exercise advice, and monitor glucose per DTG transition algorithm.

alerts.title: Missing Glucose Monitoring for DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines specify glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year for people living with HIV transitioned to DTG. The patient was switched to TLD (DTG-based) 18 months ago. There is no record of structured glucose monitoring during the first year on this regimen. The patient now presents with impaired fasting glucose and pre-diabetic HbA1c.

evidence.recommended_action: Implement guideline-recommended glucose monitoring algorithm. Schedule regular fasting glucose and/or HbA1c checks.
